summary: Async functions always return a Promise-compatible object and returned values are adopted using Promise resolution semantics.

target.notes: Use a JS-compatible async state machine and promise scheduler; do not assume Task scheduling is equivalent.

caveats: Argument evaluation occurs before the async call and may still throw synchronously.
A completed .NET awaitable may continue synchronously, unlike required JS promise-job ordering.

tests.name: plain return fulfills later
tests.input: async function f(){ return 7; } f().then(console.log); console.log('sync');
tests.expected_behavior: prints sync before 7 and f() returns a promise

tests.name: returned promise is adopted
tests.input: async function f(){ return Promise.resolve(9); } f().then(console.log);
tests.expected_behavior: fulfills with 9, not with a nested Promise object
